questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Web Performance Metrics”?
options: Web Performance Metrics means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Web Performance Metrics removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Web Performance Metrics should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
Web Performance Metrics helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.answer_key: Web Performance Metrics helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Web Performance Metrics is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Largest Contentful Paint” in this lesson?
options: Assume “Largest Contentful Paint” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Largest Contentful Paint” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Largest Contentful Paint” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
Treat “Largest Contentful Paint” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Largest Contentful Paint” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Largest Contentful Paint” under Web Performance Metrics. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Web Performance Metrics”?
options: Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
